core_obligations: Get the easy inclusion of the closure of the product set in the product of the closures (proof lines 4442-4443).
Reduce to the case where X and Y equal the closures of A and B (proof lines 4444-4445).

Prove density: for a nonempty open W of the product, the projection to X is nonempty open and hence meets A; for a chosen a in that intersection the fibre of W over a is a nonempty open of Y_{kappa(a)} whose image in Y is nonempty open, hence meets B, so W meets the product set (proof lines 4446-4459).
proof_roadmap: Density by two applications of openness (proof lines 4446-4459).
difficulty_reason: For schemes X and Y over a field k and subsets A and B, the lemma identifies the closure of the set of points of X times_k Y whose projections lie in A and B with the product of the closures of A and B (statement lines 4424-4439). One inclusion is immediate. For the other the author reduces to the case where X and Y are the closures themselves, and then argues by density: given a nonempty open W of the product, the projection of W to X is nonempty open because a scheme over a field is universally open over the base, so it meets A, and then the fibre over the chosen point a is a nonempty open subset of W whose image in Y is nonempty open, hence meets B (proof lines 4441-4459). The claim is H2: a clean density argument in which the base change of the universally open morphism to the residue field of a is what makes the second projection open as well.
